statement.p: Find the slope of the tangent line to the curve defined by 2x^{2}+6xy-3y^{5} = 53 at the point ( -7,1 ).
The slope of the curve at the point (-7, 1) is .

solution.p: Differentiating implicitly with respect to x gives 4x+6y+6x\, \frac{dy}{dx}-15y^{4}\, \frac{dy}{dx} = 0, or \left(6x-15y^{4}\right)\, \frac{dy}{dx} = -(4x+6y), and so \frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{4x+6y}{6x-15y^{4}}. Hence, the slope of the tangent line to the curve at the given point is \frac{dy}{dx} \bigg \vert _ {(x, y) = (-7, 1)} = -\frac{4\cdot \left(-7\right)+6\cdot 1}{6\cdot \left(-7\right)-15\cdot 1^{4}} \textstyle =-\frac{22}{57} .
